signals.title: EUR/USD — Geopolitical Risk + Volatility Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD has declined to 1.1578, breaking below the 1.1600 handle following reports of a vessel strike in the Strait of Hormuz and escalating US-Iran tensions. While the pair remains above its SMA20/50 cluster at 1.1493/1.1470, the options market is pricing significant protection with EUR/USD ATM IV at 7.1% vs HV30 of 4.2%, representing a +2.9% volatility risk premium. COT data shows Leveraged Funds are net short -77,671 (pctl 8, z -2.17), an extreme positioning level that typically suggests a crowded trade, yet geopolitical headlines are currently overriding technical oversold signals. The 135bp carry advantage favoring the USD (Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.4%) provides a structural floor for the dollar as risk-off sentiment builds. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; geopolitical escalation favors USD safe-haven and carry support. Catalyst: FOMC minutes release 19 Aug. Risk: De-escalation in the Middle East triggers a squeeze of the crowded spec short toward the SMA200 at 1.1634.

signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/JPY is the focal point of a G10 bilateral theme as the JPY continues its role as the broad G10 laggard with a -0.540% weekly average across 7 pairs. AUD remains the G10 leader at +0.460%, supported by a massive +335bp carry advantage (RBA 4.35% vs BoJ 1.0%) and a positive real policy rate of +0.55%. Despite retail sentiment being 90% short—a contrarian bullish signal—AUD/USD technicals show the currency in a strong position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7030/0.6995/0.6942). The spread between the G10 leader and laggard has reached 0.999%, signaling a sustained divergence that favors carry-positive AUD over the yield-depressed JPY. Trade bias: Long AUD/JPY; carry differential and G10 outperformance support the trend. Catalyst: Next BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias 100% priced. Risk: A spike in the VIX above 25 triggers a broad carry unwind, compressing the 335bp AUD/JPY advantage.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Positioning Alignment
signals.text: USD/JPY is trading at 159.73, holding below the 160.00 level that remains a key threshold for potential verbal or physical BoJ intervention. The options market is signaling high alert with a 25d Risk Reversal of -2.06, indicating a strong put skew as traders pay up for JPY strength protection despite the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry advantage. Uniquely, the VRP is negative at -1.3% (IV 7.2% vs HV30 8.5%), suggesting that while directional protection is expensive, general volatility expectations remain complacent. Speculative positioning is net short JPY at -59,526, but the WoW delta of +4,107 indicates the first signs of short-covering as price holds below the SMA20 of 160.34. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish USD/JPY; strong downside options skew and intervention risk cap upside. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 64% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 without MoF action validates the carry trade and forces an options-led squeeze.

signals.title: NZD/USD — Positioning Extreme + ESI Alignment
signals.text: NZD/USD is trading at 0.5880, supported by the SMA20 at 0.5852 but facing heavy speculative headwinds. Leveraged Funds are net short -34,031, placing NZD at a 52-week percentile of 2 (z -2.00), which represents an extreme crowded short. While the RBNZ is in a hiking cycle at 2.5%, the NZD real rate remains deeply accommodative at -1.56% due to high inflation expectations of 4.06%. The Economic Surprise Index (ESI) for NZD is a moderate +6.2, failing to provide the data-driven momentum needed to force a major squeeze of the crowded spec position. Trade bias: Neutral NZD/USD; crowded positioning limits further downside but negative real rates inhibit a recovery. Catalyst: RBNZ meeting 2 Sep — hike bias 100% priced. Risk: A significant data miss in upcoming NZ employment or trade figures validates the spec short and breaks the 0.5852 support.
